carta_page.title: Charter of Principles
carta_page.lede: The principles guiding the political action of Juventude Popular, as the youth organization of CDS-PP.
carta_page.p1: Juventude Popular defines itself as a cause-driven organization, anchored in Christian Democracy, Conservatism, and Liberalism — not as three competing factions, but as three foundations that mutually reinforce each other in how we decide. We do not choose between them based on convenience: we apply them together as a method.
carta_page.s2_title: The human person and the family
carta_page.p2: We place the human person, the family, and local communities at the center of political action, as an alternative to a State that decides everything in everyone's name. We believe in the principle of subsidiarity: what can be resolved by the family, community, or local government should not ascend to a more distant decision-making level.
carta_page.p3: We defend economic freedom and individual responsibility as conditions for progress. A State at the service of the people charges less than it needs to spend more than it should, and it is this relationship we want to invert, without abandoning solidarity with those who need it most.
carta_page.p4: We change what needs to change, preserving what already works. We do not confuse progress with rupture for the sake of rupture: a reform is only serious when it respects the accumulated experience of those who came before, not just the urgency of those who decide today.
carta_page.p5: We actively participate in European integration without losing our national identity. The European Union should be a space for cooperation between free nations, not a substitute for the sovereignty of each one.
carta_page.s6_title: A new generation at the service of the country
carta_page.p6: We do not wait for our turn to have a voice. We organize, discuss, propose, and act in more than 100 local branches, because cause-driven politics isn't made only in Lisbon—it is made in every civil parish and municipality in the country.

marcos.texto: In the same year the CDS was founded, its youth organisation was born, then named Juventude Centrista.
The organisation adopts the name Juventude Popular, an identity it keeps to this day.
JP is a member of YEPP (Youth of the European People's Party), DEMYC (Democrat Youth Community of Europe) and IYDU (International Young Democrat Union).
Over 100 active local branches from north to south and the islands, with a National Congress every two years.
